tests.title: go-git reports a failed ref write as a per-ref status that a real git push shows as remote rejected
given: a gitserver test env from newGitTestEnv with a real trunk and the handler served over HTTP
a pre-receive hook registered that rejects every update with the text 'nope: blocked'
a local clone with one new commit on branch feature
tests.when: git push is run from the clone to the hub for refs/heads/feature
then: git push exits non-zero
client output contains 'remote rejected' and 'nope: blocked'
client output shows unpack ok semantics (no 'unpack failed')
the trunk's refs/heads/feature does not exist
the HTTP response status of the receive-pack POST is 200
tests.pseudocode: RegisterPreReceiveHook(func(...) error { return errors.New('nope: blocked') }); out, err := gitPush(clone, 'feature'); assert err != nil; assert contains(out,'remote rejected'); assert contains(out,'nope: blocked'); assert refMissing(trunk,'refs/heads/feature')

tests.title: With no hook, or after registering nil, pushes behave as before; a nil-returning hook lets the ref be written
given: a gitserver test env
tests.when: a push is made with no hook, then with a hook returning nil, then after RegisterPreReceiveHook(nil) following a rejecting hook
then: all three pushes succeed
after each push the trunk ref holds the pushed commit
the cleared rejecting hook is no longer consulted
tests.pseudocode: push -> assert ref==sha1; Register(allowAll); push -> assert ref==sha2; Register(rejectAll); Register(nil); push -> assert ref==sha3

tests.title: The hook is called once per ref update in command order with request context, db, slug, actor and update
given: a recording pre-receive hook that returns nil
an authenticated request with apikit.AuthInfo for user u1 injected by the middleware
a push that creates branch a, updates branch b and deletes branch c
tests.when: git push is run with all three updates in one request
then: the hook is called exactly three times
calls arrive in the same order as the commands
each call carries slug, a non-nil context that is cancelled when the request ends, the *sql.DB, actor u1 and the ref name, old hash and new hash of its command
at call time the new commit object is already readable from the trunk and the ref has not yet been written
with an unauthenticated test context the actor argument is nil-safe and the hook is still called
tests.pseudocode: calls=[]; hook=func(ctx,db,slug,actor,upd){ calls=append(calls,{slug,actor,upd,hasObj(trunk,upd.New),refVal(trunk,upd.Name)}); return nil }; push(a,b,c); assert names(calls)==['a','b','c']; assert calls[0].hasObj

tests.title: A hook rejecting one of two refs leaves the other written and reports only the rejected ref's message
given: a hook that rejects refs/heads/blocked with 'blocked by policy' and accepts refs/heads/open
a clone with commits on both branches
tests.when: one git push sends both branches to the hub handler
then: refs/heads/open in the trunk equals the pushed commit
refs/heads/blocked is unchanged (absent or at its old value)
client output contains 'blocked by policy' attached to blocked
client output has no rejection message for open
tests.pseudocode: push(both); assert ref(open)==sha; assert ref(blocked)==old; assert out contains 'blocked by policy'; assert not rejectedLine(out,'open')

tests.title: The storer wrapper consults the hook on every reference write and removal, still hides PackfileWriter, and gitserver does not import carrypatch
given: thinPackSafeStorer wrapping a real repo storer with a recording hook bound to a request context and actor
tests.when: SetReference, CheckAndSetReference and RemoveReference are called on the wrapper, and the dependency list of internal/gitserver is inspected
then: each reference-writing and removing method calls the hook exactly once before delegating
a hook error is returned and the underlying storer is not modified
the wrapper does not expose a PackfileWriter method (type assertion to storer.PackfileWriter fails)
go list -deps for internal/gitserver contains no internal/carrypatch package
tests.pseudocode: w := thinPackSafeStorer{...}; _,ok := any(w).(storer.PackfileWriter); assert !ok; assert w.SetReference(ref)==hookErr when hook rejects; deps := goListDeps('./internal/gitserver'); assert none contains 'internal/carrypatch'

tests.title: A client that does not request report-status still has the hook's rejection enforced but gets no per-ref message
given: a hook that rejects refs/heads/feature with 'denied here'
a hand-built receive-pack request body without the report-status capability
tests.when: the request is POSTed to the receive-pack handler
then: the trunk's refs/heads/feature is unchanged
the response body contains no 'ng' line and no 'denied here' text
tests.pseudocode: body := encodeUpdateRequest(cmds, caps=[]); resp := post(body); assert ref(feature)==old; assert !contains(resp.body,'denied here')

tests.title: An empty-body receive-pack request does not call the pre-receive hook
given: a counting pre-receive hook
tests.when: POST /git/<slug>/git-receive-pack is sent with an empty body
then: the response is the existing no-op response
the hook call count is 0
tests.pseudocode: post(emptyBody); assert hookCalls==0

tests.title: A panicking pre-receive hook gets no special recovery from the git server
given: a hook that panics
the handler mounted the same way as in existing tests (with the framework's normal recovery behaviour)
tests.when: a push with one ref update is sent
then: the handler adds no recover of its own; the outcome is the same as for any other handler panic (existing behaviour)
no accepted-ref side effects (audit event, post-push hook) occur
tests.pseudocode: Register(panicHook); assertPanicHandledLikeOtherHandlers(push()); assert auditCount==0 && postHookCalls==0

tests.title: info/refs, clone, fetch and pushes to unregistered branches, integration branch, tags, other refs and standard workspaces are unchanged with the carry-patch hook wired
given: the carry-patch pre-receive hook registered
a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and a standard workspace
a registered patch branch in the carry_patch workspace
tests.when: info/refs is requested, the repo is cloned and fetched, and pushes are made to an unregistered branch, the integration branch, a tag, refs/notes/x in the carry_patch workspace, and a branch in the standard workspace
then: the advertisement, clone and fetch succeed with the same refs as before
every one of those pushes succeeds and the refs are written
no origin push occurs
tests.pseudocode: assert advertise ok; clone ok; for ref in [feature,integration,tag v1,refs/notes/x]: assert push(ref).ok && ref written; assert push(stdBranch).ok

tests.title: PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is enabled only by the exact string true
given: a GetVariableFunc stub returning controlled values
tests.when: the flag parser is evaluated with unset, 'true', 'True', 'TRUE', '1', ' true', empty string and a lookup error
then: only 'true' yields enabled
every other input including the lookup error yields disabled
tests.pseudocode: table: {unset:false,'true':true,'True':false,'1':false,err:false}; for each: assert pushPatchesEnabled(get)==expected

tests.title: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE uses spec 20's parsing and both variables are re-read on every controlled ref update
given: a counting GetVariableFunc over a real variable store
a registered patch branch in a carry_patch workspace
tests.when: pushes are made with the source unset, 'garbage', and a lookup error (all meaning hub), then the variable is changed to origin between two pushes
then: unset, unrecognised and error values behave as hub (no rejection)
after PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE changes to origin the very next push is rejected without restarting anything
both variables are read once per controlled ref update
tests.pseudocode: push1 ok under unset; set(PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE,'origin'); push2 rejected; assert getCalls per update >= 2 for both names

tests.title: Push control applies to refs/heads/<name> matching a non-deleted patch row of a carry_patch workspace
given: a carry_patch workspace with integration_branch 'main-int' and patches rows with statuses active, pending and conflict
source origin with forwarding off
tests.when: the carry-patch hook is invoked for each of those branches
then: each call returns a non-nil rejection error showing control applied
tests.pseudocode: for b in [active,pending,conflict]: assert hook(ctx,db,slug,actor,update(refs/heads/+b)) != nil

tests.title: Updates the control does not apply to are let through with no origin push
given: source origin, forwarding on, a recording origin push function and a bare origin
a carry_patch workspace with a patch row status deleted, a patch row named like the integration branch, and a standard workspace
tests.when: the hook is invoked for the deleted-status branch, the integration branch, a branch with no row, refs/tags/v1, refs/notes/x and a branch in the standard workspace
then: every call returns nil
no push reaches the origin bare repository
for a real push the hub writes each ref
tests.pseudocode: for u in cases: assert hook(u)==nil; assert originRefs(bare)==[]

tests.title: A standard-mode workspace push reads neither variable
given: a standard-mode workspace
a GetVariableFunc stub counting calls
tests.when: the hook is invoked for updates to several refs in a push to that workspace
then: the hook returns nil each time
the GetVariableFunc call count is 0
tests.pseudocode: assert hook(...)==nil; assert getVarCalls==0

tests.title: Reject mode refuses a create and an update of a registered patch branch with the origin message
given: carry_patch workspace, git_url https://example.com/fork.git, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN unset
registered patch branch 'p1' existing at commit A on the hub
tests.when: git push creates registered branch 'p2' (a row exists, ref absent), then git push updates p1 to commit B
then: both pushes fail with 'remote rejected' and 'branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'
hub p1 still equals A and hub p2 does not exist
tests.pseudocode: assert contains(out,'branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'); assert ref(p1)==A; assert refMissing(p2)

tests.title: Userinfo in git_url never appears in the rejection message
given: workspaces.git_url 'https://user:s3cret@example.com/fork.git'
reject mode applies
tests.when: the hook rejects an update
then: the message is 'branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'
the message contains neither 'user' as credential nor 's3cret' nor '@'
tests.pseudocode: err := hook(...); assert err.Error()=='branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'

tests.title: For any git_url with userinfo the rejection message is credential-free
given: reject mode applies
tests.when: for any generated URL scheme, username, password (including characters like ':' '%' '!') host and path, stored as git_url with user:password@ userinfo
then: the rejection message never contains the username:password text
the message equals the template with the URL rendered without userinfo
tests.pseudocode: for url in gen_urls_with_userinfo(): msg := hook(...).Error(); assert !contains(msg, password); assert msg == fmt('branch is synced from origin; push to %s instead', stripUserinfo(url))

tests.title: Reject mode refuses the deletion of a registered patch branch
given: reject mode, registered patch branch p1 present on the hub
tests.when: git push origin :refs/heads/p1 is run against the hub
then: the client sees 'remote rejected' with the origin message
hub p1 still exists at its old commit
tests.pseudocode: out := gitPush(':refs/heads/p1'); assert contains(out,'branch is synced from origin'); assert ref(p1)==old

tests.title: A push mixing a registered branch, an unregistered branch and a tag rejects only the registered branch
given: reject mode
commits for registered branch p1, unregistered branch feature and tag v1
tests.when: a single git push sends all three
then: only p1 shows remote rejected
feature and v1 exist in the hub trunk
p1 unchanged
tests.pseudocode: out := push(p1,feature,v1); assert rejectedRefs(out)==['refs/heads/p1']; assert ref(feature)&&tag(v1)

tests.title: A rejection is logged at info level with slug, branch and user, and the HTTP status is 200
given: reject mode
a captured logger
authenticated user id 'u-42', and a second run with no auth info
tests.when: a push of a registered patch branch is rejected
then: the HTTP response status is 200
an info-level record contains slug, branch and user 'u-42'
without auth info the user field is 'unknown'
tests.pseudocode: resp := post(...); assert resp.Status==200; rec := logs.Find(INFO,'rejected'); assert rec.slug && rec.branch && rec.user=='u-42'

tests.title: Forward mode pushes a create and a fast-forward update to a local bare origin before writing the hub ref
given: trunk's origin remote is a local bare repository
source origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, registered patch branch p1
tests.when: git push creates p1 at commit A, then pushes fast-forward commit B
then: after the first push p1 equals A in both the hub trunk and the bare origin
after the second push p1 equals B in both
the origin received the commit before the hub ref was written (hook returns after origin has the ref)
an already-up-to-date forward (pushing a commit the origin already has) succeeds
tests.pseudocode: push(A); assert ref(trunk,p1)==A && ref(bare,p1)==A; push(B); assert both==B; seedOrigin(C); push(C); assert ok

tests.title: The temporary refs/hub/forward/<branch> ref is absent after a successful and after a failed forward
given: forward mode with a local bare origin
tests.when: one forward succeeds and one fails because the origin is ahead (non-fast-forward)
then: after each, no ref under refs/hub/forward/ exists in the trunk
during the forward the push is made from the temporary ref or a hash source that resolves the unreferenced commit
tests.pseudocode: push(ok); assert refsWithPrefix(trunk,'refs/hub/forward/')==[]; push(nonff); assert refsWithPrefix(trunk,'refs/hub/forward/')==[]

tests.title: Forward uses ResolveCloneAuth credentials, a non-force refspec and a 120 second deadline
given: an injected credential resolver recording its calls and a push function seam recording PushOptions and context
tests.when: the hook forwards an update
then: the resolver is called with the workspace slug
PushOptions has RemoteName origin, Force false and a refspec with no leading '+'
the context passed to the push has a deadline about 120 seconds from now
tests.pseudocode: opts, ctx := captured; assert opts.Force==false; assert !startsWith(opts.RefSpecs[0],'+'); assert 119s < deadline(ctx)-now <= 120s

tests.title: Credential resolution failure rejects the ref without contacting origin
given: forward mode
a resolver returning an error
a bare origin
tests.when: the hook is invoked for a registered branch update
then: the returned error text is exactly 'failed to resolve origin credentials'
the bare origin receives nothing
through a real push the hub ref is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: err := hook(...); assert err.Error()=='failed to resolve origin credentials'; assert originRefs==[]

tests.title: A non-fast-forward forward is rejected with the origin error text and leaves hub and fork refs unchanged
given: forward mode with a local bare origin whose p1 has moved ahead with a commit the hub lacks
hub p1 at commit A
tests.when: git push sends a different commit B on p1
then: the client shows 'remote rejected' with text starting 'origin rejected push: ' including the go-git non-fast-forward error
hub p1 still equals A
origin p1 still equals its own tip
the hook returned a non-nil error
tests.pseudocode: out := push(B); assert contains(out,'origin rejected push: '); assert ref(trunk,p1)==A; assert ref(bare,p1)==originTip

tests.title: An unreachable origin rejects the update, leaves the hub ref unchanged and logs a warning without userinfo
given: forward mode where the origin remote URL is a nonexistent path or URL containing user:pw@
a captured logger
tests.when: git push updates registered branch p1
then: the per-ref message starts with 'origin rejected push: ' and contains no 'pw' credential text
hub p1 is unchanged
a warn-level record contains slug, branch, user and the credential-free error
tests.pseudocode: out := push(); assert contains(out,'origin rejected push: '); assert !contains(out,'pw'); rec := logs.Find(WARN); assert rec.slug && rec.branch && rec.user && !contains(rec.error,'pw')

tests.title: Forward mode rejects deleting a registered patch branch without contacting origin
given: forward mode, p1 exists on both hub and local bare origin
tests.when: git push :refs/heads/p1 is run
then: the client shows 'branch is synced from origin; delete it on the fork instead'
hub p1 and origin p1 still exist
no push was attempted against origin
tests.pseudocode: out := push(':p1'); assert contains(out,'branch is synced from origin; delete it on the fork instead'); assert exists(trunk,p1)&&exists(bare,p1)

tests.title: A mixed push forwards the patch branch and passes an unregistered branch through unchanged
given: forward mode with local bare origin
registered p1 and unregistered feature
tests.when: one git push sends both
then: both refs are written on the hub
p1 exists on the origin bare repository
feature does not exist on the origin
tests.pseudocode: push(p1,feature); assert ref(trunk,p1)&&ref(trunk,feature); assert exists(bare,p1); assert !exists(bare,feature)

tests.title: A ref is accepted when its report-status entry is ok, or, with no report, unless the hook rejected it
given: a ReportStatus with entries ok for refs/heads/a and an error string for refs/heads/b
a nil report with a hook-rejected set containing refs/heads/c
tests.when: the accepted-commands classifier runs on both inputs
then: with the report only a is accepted
with no report, every command except c is accepted
tests.pseudocode: assert names(accepted(cmds,rs,nil))==['a']; assert names(accepted(cmds,nil,{c}))==['a','b']

tests.title: A mixed push calls the post-push hook with accepted branches only and audits only the accepted ref
given: a hook rejecting refs/heads/p1
a recording post-push hook and audit emitter
a deletion of refs/heads/old included in the push and accepted
tests.when: one git push sends p1, feature and the delete of old
then: post-push hook receives ['feature'] only (delete excluded, p1 excluded)
hub.git.push has refs_updated listing feature and the accepted delete only, not p1
tests.pseudocode: push(p1,feature,':old'); assert postHookBranches==['feature']; assert 'refs/heads/p1' not in event.refs_updated; assert 'refs/heads/feature' in event.refs_updated

tests.title: A push where nothing was accepted emits no audit event and runs no post-push hook or rebuild
given: reject mode with the real carry-patch post-push hook and a job queue
a recording audit emitter
tests.when: git push of only a registered patch branch is rejected
then: no hub.git.push event is emitted
the post-push hook is not called
no rebuild job is enqueued
HTTP status is 200
tests.pseudocode: push(p1); wait(); assert events==[]; assert hookCalls==0; assert queue.len()==0

tests.title: updateHeadSHA still reads the trunk HEAD for every push including rejected-only pushes
given: a workspace whose head_sha is stale
a trunk whose HEAD changed through an accepted push, and a second rejected-only push
tests.when: the receive-pack handler finishes each push
then: head_sha equals the trunk HEAD after the accepted push
after the rejected-only push head_sha equals the current trunk HEAD (unchanged and harmless)
tests.pseudocode: push(ok); assert db.head_sha==trunkHEAD; push(rejected); assert db.head_sha==trunkHEAD

tests.title: For any push, side effects cover a subset of ref updates whose status is ok
given: a stub receive session producing arbitrary per-command statuses
tests.when: for any list of commands (create, update, delete, branches, tags) with any assignment of ok or error statuses and any hook-rejection subset
then: the audited refs and the post-push branches are subsets of the ok commands
no command with non-ok status ever appears in either
no event is emitted when the ok set is empty
tests.pseudocode: for cmds,statuses in gen(): accepted := classify(cmds,statuses); assert set(audited) <= set(ok(cmds,statuses)); assert set(postBranches) <= set(branchesOf(ok)); assert (len(ok)==0) == (eventsEmitted==0)

tests.title: Hub-mode mirror force-pushes a created branch and a rewritten branch to the local bare origin
given: hub mode (source unset), PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, local bare origin, registered patch branch p1
post-push hook built with credential resolver, workspace root and emitter
tests.when: p1 is pushed (create), then rewritten with a force push to a diverging commit
then: after the first hook run origin p1 equals the hub tip
after the rewrite origin p1 equals the new hub tip (forced update)
the refspec used is '+refs/heads/p1:refs/heads/p1' with a 120 second deadline
tests.pseudocode: hook(db,slug,['p1']); assert ref(bare,p1)==ref(trunk,p1); rewrite(); hook(db,slug,['p1']); assert ref(bare,p1)==newTip

tests.title: The rebuild enqueue runs first and the mirror runs afterwards, including when AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is false
given: hub mode with forwarding on, a recording queue and a local bare origin
scenarios: rebuild enqueued, AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false, deduplicated enqueue
tests.when: the post-push hook runs for registered branch p1
then: in the enqueue scenario the enqueue is observed before the origin push
with AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false no job is enqueued but origin receives p1
with a deduplicated enqueue origin still receives p1
both happen in the single hook goroutine
tests.pseudocode: order := recordOrder(queue, originPush); assert order==['enqueue','mirror']; setVar(AUTO,'false'); run; assert queue.len()==0 && exists(bare,p1)

tests.title: A failing mirror does not prevent the rebuild or the other branches, and an enqueue failure does not stop the mirror
given: hub mode with forwarding on
a local bare origin with a pre-receive hook refusing branch p2
two registered branches p1 and p2 in one push
a second run where the queue enqueue returns an error
tests.when: the post-push hook runs with ['p1','p2'] and then with a failing queue
then: a rebuild job is enqueued despite the p2 failure
p1 is mirrored to origin and p2 is not
the hook does not panic or return a failure
with the failing queue both branches are still attempted for mirroring
no retry occurs (the origin sees one attempt per branch)
tests.pseudocode: hook(db,slug,['p1','p2']); assert queue.len()==1; assert exists(bare,p1) && !exists(bare,p2); queue.failNext(); hook(...); assert exists(bare,p1)

tests.title: No mirror for disabled variable, origin source, unregistered branch, integration branch or standard workspace
given: a local bare origin
registered branch p1 and the integration branch in a carry_patch workspace and a standard workspace
tests.when: the post-push hook runs in each case: variable unset, variable 'True', source origin with variable true, branch 'feature' unregistered, the integration branch, and the standard workspace
then: the origin bare repository receives no ref in every case
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: setup(case); hook(db,slug,[branch]); assert originRefs(bare)==[]

tests.title: Branch deletions are never mirrored
given: hub mode with forwarding on and p1 present on the origin
tests.when: a push that deletes registered branch p1 is accepted and the post-push hook is invoked through handleReceivePack
then: the post-push hook receives no branches for the delete
origin p1 is not deleted
tests.pseudocode: push(':p1'); assert hookBranches==[]; assert exists(bare,p1)

tests.title: Mirror works only when its dependencies are supplied; with any nil it is disabled and rebuild behaviour is unchanged
given: hub mode with forwarding on and a local bare origin
tests.when: NewPostPushRebuildHook is built with all dependencies, and then with each of the credential resolver, workspace root (empty) and emitter nil in turn
then: with all supplied origin receives the branch
with any one nil origin receives nothing and the rebuild job is still enqueued as before with SubmittedBy system:push-hook
tests.pseudocode: for deps in [all, nilResolver, emptyRoot, nilEmitter]: hook := New(queue,get,deps...); hook(db,slug,['p1']); assert queue.len()==1; assert exists(bare,p1)==(deps==all)

tests.title: A mirror failure emits hub.patch.mirror_failed with the required fields and credential-free error
given: a recording emitter and an origin whose error text contains https://user:pw@host/repo.git
tests.when: the mirror of branch p1 fails
then: one event of type hub.patch.mirror_failed is emitted
resource_type is patch, action is mirror, actor_type is system, workspace slug is set
metadata contains branch_name p1 and error without 'user:pw@'
tests.pseudocode: ev := emitter.events[0]; assert ev.Type=='hub.patch.mirror_failed'; assert ev.ResourceType=='patch' && ev.Action=='mirror' && ev.ActorType=='system'; assert ev.Metadata.branch_name=='p1'; assert !contains(ev.Metadata.error,'pw')

tests.title: The audit package defines the hub.patch.mirror_failed constant next to EventRebuildFollowup
given: internal/audit/types.go
tests.when: the constant is referenced and the source is read
then: the constant's value is 'hub.patch.mirror_failed'
it is declared adjacent to EventRebuildFollowup
tests.pseudocode: assert audit.EventPatchMirrorFailed=='hub.patch.mirror_failed'; assert adjacent(src,'EventRebuildFollowup','hub.patch.mirror_failed')

tests.title: A successful mirror logs at info and emits nothing; a failed mirror logs at warn with slug, branch and error
given: a captured logger and a recording emitter
a working local bare origin and a failing origin
tests.when: the mirror runs for a good origin, then for a failing origin
then: success: an info record is written and no event is emitted
failure: a warn record contains slug, branch and the error
tests.pseudocode: mirror(good); assert logs.Has(INFO) && emitter.events==[]; mirror(bad); assert logs.Find(WARN).slug && .branch && .error

tests.title: A nil emitter or an emitter that errors changes nothing else about the mirror outcome
given: hub mode with forwarding on, branches p1 (failing) and p2 (succeeding)
one run with an emitter returning an error on every emit and one run with a nil emitter passed through a test seam
tests.when: the post-push hook runs
then: no panic
p2 is mirrored and the rebuild job is enqueued in both runs
the emit error is logged
with a nil emitter no emission is attempted
tests.pseudocode: run(errEmitter); assert exists(bare,p2) && queue.len()==1; assert logs.Has('emit'); run(nilEmitter); assert exists(bare,p2)

tests.title: A failure while deciding whether control applies lets the update through with a warning
given: a carry_patch workspace with source origin
stubs that fail one at a time: the workspace-mode query, a variable lookup returning an unexpected failure beyond defaults, and the patches registration query
tests.when: the hook is invoked for a registered branch update under each failure
then: the hook returns nil in each case
a warn-level record is logged each time
a real push in this state writes the hub ref
tests.pseudocode: for failure in [modeQuery,patchQuery,variableErr]: assert hook(...)==nil; assert logs.Has(WARN)

tests.title: cmd/af-hub wiring registers the carry-patch pre-receive hook and builds the post-push hook with credentials, workspace root and emitter
given: the app wiring function from cmd/af-hub run against a test database and temporary workspace root
tests.when: after wiring, a push of a registered branch is made in origin mode, and a hub-mode push with forwarding on is made
then: the origin-mode push is rejected with the origin message (pre-receive hook registered)
the hub-mode push reaches the local bare origin (post-push hook has mirror dependencies)
the wiring source uses store.GetVariableValue and workspace.ResolveCloneAuth and declares no local auth struct
tests.pseudocode: app := wire(); assert contains(push(origin mode),'branch is synced from origin'); assert exists(bare,p1) after hub-mode push

tests.title: docs/api.md documents the variable, the three push behaviours, per-ref messages, accepted-refs-only rule and mirror_failed event
given: docs/api.md
tests.when: the file is searched
then: the Workspace Variables Reference lists PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN
the git push section mentions 'branch is synced from origin; push to', 'origin rejected push:', 'failed to resolve origin credentials' and accepted refs only
hub.patch.mirror_failed is documented
tests.pseudocode: for s in strings: assert contains(read('docs/api.md'), s)

tests.title: docs/openapi.yaml and docs/architecture.md describe the variable, rejections and pre-receive hook
given: docs/openapi.yaml and docs/architecture.md
tests.when: the files are searched
then: openapi mentions PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN and the rejections in the receive-pack route description
architecture.md git server section mentions the pre-receive hook
tests.pseudocode: assert contains(openapi,'PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN'); assert contains(arch,'pre-receive')

tests.title: carry_patch_workflow.md gets the variable entry and the updated note, while configuration.md and cli.md are unchanged
given: docs/carry_patch_workflow.md, docs/configuration.md and docs/cli.md compared with the base revision
tests.when: the files are searched and diffed
then: the Configuration section lists PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN
the spec 20 note describes rejection, forwarding and mirroring

tests.title: A developer's push to a registered patch branch in origin mode is rejected end to end
given: a running hub handler with real gitserver, carry-patch hooks, database and trunk
carry_patch workspace, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN unset, git_url with userinfo
registered branch p1
tests.when: a real git push updates p1
then: git shows 'remote rejected' with 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url without userinfo> instead'
hub p1 is unchanged
no hub.git.push event is emitted and no post-push hook or rebuild runs

tests.title: A push to a registered patch branch in origin mode with forwarding on reaches both fork and hub
given: running hub with real gitserver, carry-patch hooks, database and trunk
local bare repository as the trunk's origin
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, registered branch p1
tests.when: a real git push sends a new commit on p1
then: the push succeeds
p1 is at the same commit on the bare origin and the hub trunk
no refs/hub/forward/* remains
hub.git.push is emitted listing refs/heads/p1 and the post-push hook runs

tests.title: A forward refused by the fork as non-fast-forward leaves the hub ref unchanged
given: running hub with real gitserver and carry-patch hooks
local bare origin whose p1 is ahead of the pushed commit's history
origin mode with forwarding on, a captured logger
tests.when: a real git push sends p1 behind the fork's p1
then: git shows 'remote rejected' with 'origin rejected push: ' and the origin error text
hub p1 and origin p1 are unchanged
the temporary forward ref is gone
a warn record is logged

tests.title: A hub-mode push of a registered patch branch is accepted, rebuilt and mirrored to the fork
given: running hub with real gitserver, post-push rebuild hook with credentials, workspace root and emitter, and a real queue
local bare origin, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, registered branch p1
tests.when: a real git push sends commits on p1
then: the push succeeds and hub p1 holds the commit
a rebuild job with SubmittedBy system:push-hook is enqueued
the bare origin holds p1 at the hub tip

tests.title: A failed mirror is reported through hub.patch.mirror_failed while the push, rebuild and other branch succeed
given: running hub with real gitserver, post-push hook and a recording audit emitter
local bare origin with a hook refusing p2
hub mode, forwarding on, registered branches p1 and p2
tests.when: a real git push sends p1 and p2
then: the push succeeds with HTTP 200
a rebuild job is enqueued
p1 exists on the origin and p2 does not
one hub.patch.mirror_failed event has resource_type patch, action mirror, actor_type system, slug and metadata branch_name p2 with credential-free error

tests.title: After registration and sync of a fork-only branch, a mixed push rejects only the registered branch
given: a fork-only branch registered through POST /workspaces/:slug/patches in origin mode
the sync job has created the hub patch branch from the fork
real gitserver, hooks, database and local bare origin
tests.when: a real git push sends the registered branch, an unregistered branch and a tag
then: the registered branch shows remote rejected with the origin message
the unregistered branch and tag are written on the hub
hub.git.push lists only those accepted refs and the post-push hook receives only the unregistered branch
the HTTP status is 200
